column6: Scope note: session 330 material and circulating names diverge from shipped headers; verify against the SDK first.
set() on a masked cooperative-tensor element does nothing and get() returns 0 - the wrong identity for max reductions.
A macOS deployment target below 26.2 makes MLX drop every accelerated kernel behind only a CMake warning.
The Metal toolchain cryptex path embeds a build-specific token; resolve it with xcrun, never paste it into scripts.
matmul_mode defaults to mode::multiply, not accumulate - see the 3.5 K-loop trap.
matmul2d's default mode is multiply and its exact semantics are not fully settled in the docs.
A K loop left in the default multiply mode overwrites instead of accumulating, keeping only the last tile's product.
execution_simdgroups<N>, simdGroupsPerTG and descriptor (m,n) must agree; mismatch corrupts tiles like a numerics bug.
Circulating material calls tensor_offset a descriptor; in the header it is a Tag.
static_slice does not exist in the SDK; the real spelling is a templated slice.
The 4-bit path is a pointer cast to tensor<int4b_format>; the 26.x matmul2d op does the unpacking itself.
Masked-element set/get silently no-op or return zero, and a widely cited guard method name does not exist.
Verified: set() on a masked element is a no-op and get() returns zero; operator[] is entirely unchecked.
MLX writes cooperative tensors through unchecked operator[] and never calls is_valid_element, relying on known layouts.
MLX hardcodes an undocumented fragment linearisation (kElemsPerFrag); a toolchain change could silently break it.
reduce_rows' identity defaults to sum_identity (zero) regardless of the operation you pass.
Naked exp() in a hand-written softmax overflows above ~88 fp32 / ~11 fp16; subtract the running max first.
The guide's central trap: the default reduction identity silently clamps every negative row max to zero.
TOC: cooperative tensors are not zero-initialised; they hold undefined register data.
TOC: the reduce_rows identity default silently computes max(0,row).
TOC: NAX is new and still settling; expect churn.
Never hardcode the MetalToolchain cryptex path; the version token differs per machine - resolve via xcrun.
Default macOS builds target below 26.2, so MLX drops all NAX kernels with just a CMake warning (PRs #3622, #3824).
get_destination_cooperative_tensor has a single no-argument overload; no predicate, no conversion, unlike inputs.
Skip the is_compatible_as_left_input check and an incompatible layout converts undiagnosed - wrong data, no error.
The shipping header's example loop writes a comma where a semicolon belongs; pasted verbatim it will not compile.
Cooperative tensors are not zero-initialised; accumulate into one unwritten and you add register garbage.
Uninitialised cooperative tensors often read 0 on a fresh pipeline and garbage on the next launch; it ships, then fails.
The reduce_rows identity default is zero for every operation, including max.
reduce_rows(S,rowMax,max) compiles and computes max(0,row); every all-negative row silently becomes zero.
Apple's map_iterator example passes the tensor where an iterator is required and drops a semicolon; do not paste it.
execution_threadgroup does not exist; the header admits only execution_threads<1> and execution_simdgroups<N>.
slice(a,b) takes (column,row) while matmul2d_descriptor takes (rows,columns); mixed conventions slice the wrong tiles.
The per-simdgroup if must not make run() non-uniform; divergent execution of the op is undefined behaviour.
Code comment: reduce_rows takes four arguments here - the identity is not optional in practice.
The three-argument reduce_rows in flash attention computes max(0,row); attention logits are frequently all-negative.
Code comment: four arguments; three would silently compute max(0,row).
Dispatch fewer threads than the execution scope declares and the op reads non-participating lanes; no validation exists.
Custom-kernel src is the body only; includes, using-declarations and descriptor constexprs must go in helper_src.
coreai.authoring Metal-kernel APIs are experimental and subject to change; pin your coreai-torch version.
NAX is new and still settling; expect kernel, gate and semantics churn across releases.
The headline speedup is one matmul shape on one machine; do not carry it into a different context.
